slides.title: Shared Ownership with std::shared_ptr
slides.prompt: std::shared_ptr enables shared ownership across multiple smart pointers using reference counting. The resource is destroyed when the final std::shared_ptr referencing it goes out of scope.

slides.title: Creating shared_ptr
slides.prompt: Fill in the preferred function used to construct a std::shared_ptr efficiently.

slides.title: Reference Counting Control Block
slides.prompt: What extra structure does std::shared_ptr maintain alongside the managed object?
options: A dynamic Control Block containing shared reference count, weak reference count, and deleter
A static global hash table of alive pointers
A thread mutex table for every variable access
A binary search tree tracking scopes
slides.correctAnswer: A dynamic Control Block containing shared reference count, shared reference count, weak reference count, and deleter

slides.title: Checking Use Count
slides.prompt: Fill in the member function that returns the current number of shared_ptr instances managing the resource.

slides.title: std::make_shared Efficiency
slides.prompt: Why is std::make_shared preferred over using std::shared_ptr(new T())?
options: Combines object allocation and control block allocation into a single memory block
slides.correctAnswer: Combines object allocation and control block allocation into a single memory block

slides.title: Checking Pointer Validity
slides.prompt: Fill in the boolean check idiom to determine if a shared_ptr holds a valid object.
slides.codeSnippet: if (___ptr) { /* Object exists and pointer is not null */ }

slides.title: Thread Safety of std::shared_ptr
slides.prompt: Which part of std::shared_ptr is guaranteed to be thread-safe automatically?
options: Atomic updates to the reference count in the control block
Concurrent writes to the underlying managed object value
Re-assigning the same shared_ptr variable from multiple threads simultaneously without locks
slides.correctAnswer: Atomic updates to the reference count in the control block

slides.title: Shared Pointer Aliasing Constructor
slides.prompt: Fill in the constructor mode that allows a shared_ptr to share ownership of one object while pointing to a member inside it.

slides.title: Performance Overhead of shared_ptr
slides.prompt: Compared to std::unique_ptr, what additional runtime costs does std::shared_ptr incur?
options: Atomic increment/decrement operations on reference count and indirect heap control block storage
Memory re-allocation on every pointer dereference
Stack frame overhead on every function call
slides.correctAnswer: Atomic increment/decrement operations on reference count and indirect heap control block storage

slides.title: Unique Check Method
slides.prompt: Fill in the function check to verify if a shared_ptr is the sole owner (deprecated in C++20, but conceptually checked via use_count()==1).
